Why mint feels cold

Hardest passage: two inputs, one channel

Read the relationship with decorative headings hidden. The leaf, ice and channel must retain their identities through the changing connection. The figure is explicitly conceptual; these are not observed molecular images or measured response traces.

Initial

Initial: cooling cue is connected to the anchored channel print. Menthol path remains incomplete context.

Difficult intermediate

Difficult intermediate: second input approaches the same channel; the inactive ice is selectively softened. Both source objects survive.

Resolved

Resolved: both input categories are visible at the same labeled channel; response is conceptual, not a measured amplitude.

Review boundary

Assess source specificity, connected explanation, the difficult intermediate, text contrast, textures and phone-size clarity. Moving focus hunt, mechanical jitter, edge boil, transition blur, camera timing and sound are not demonstrated by stills. Only approval of these exact images permits their moving test. That test will validate its passage only; the final episode still needs one complete preview.
